page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance built on the ARMv9 AWS Graviton4 platform. It features 192 dedicated physical cores running at 2.7 GHz using the ARM Neoverse-V2 architecture, without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 1,536 GB of DDR5 RAM, establishing an 8 GB per core memory profile. The bare-metal design provides direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead, paired with 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Local ephemeral storage is provided via 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, while no discrete GPUs are present. In synthetic and memory benchmarks, the platform demonstrates massive throughput, achieving top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-core Geekbench evaluations, and high-volume memory bandwidth measurements reaching 895.65 GB/sec for large-block read operations. Software compilation via Clang and multi-threaded decompression tests similarly place in the upper performance tier.

Tradeoffs emerge between single-threaded clock limitations and extensive parallelism. Single-core Geekbench and stress-ng scores align with mid-range baselines, and CPU-based LLM token generation remains slow due to the absence of dedicated hardware accelerators. In contrast, in-memory operations and database transactions exhibit high efficiency, marked by 374.08 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier PassMark database scores.

From an infrastructure cost efficiency standpoint, the dense aggregation of 192 dedicated Graviton4 cores, massive DDR5 capacity, and integrated 11.4 TB NVMe tier minimizes per-gigabyte memory costs for large installations. The platform is best matched for enterprise in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale data transformation, and heavy web serving environments.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance featuring 192 dedicated physical cores powered by the 2.7 GHz ARMv9 AWS Graviton4 (Neoverse-V2) processor. The architecture delivers 1,536 GB of high-bandwidth DDR5 memory alongside 11,400 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps baseline networking, operating without a hypervisor. While single-thread execution rates and CPU-only LLM generation speeds remain moderate, the system excels across parallel and memory-intensive benchmarks, recording top-tier multi-core compute throughput, Clang compilation speeds, and over 374 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking discrete GPUs, it is tailored for dense transactional workloads, distributed memory caches, massive relational or NoSQL database platforms, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
